title: Deser and Arnowitt graviton essay
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Deser and Arnowitt graviton essay, about 1954 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: The pair wrote a paper about these theoretical gravitons in their 1954 winning essay for the Gravity Research Foundation.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1954 two physicists, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt, won the essay prize of the Gravity Research Foundation, a group that held a yearly contest for writing on gravity, with a paper about gravitons, theoretical particles thought to carry the force of gravity. He sets it beside a writer named Michael Gladish and a piece called "The G Engines Are Coming," as a sign that serious scientists of the 1950s were working on gravity in ways some connect to antigravity flight.
